n3_diagnosis.question: what in the model makes N = 3 queue more than the measurement?
n3_diagnosis.mechanism: IT IS NOT THE QUEUE, IT IS THE QUEUEING QUANTUM. The model's p50 is right at both N: 0.264 s simulated at N = 3 against StudyE10c's measured 0.25-0.30 s, and 0.144 s at N = 1 against its 0.14-0.15 s. What differs is what a request pays when it is NOT admitted at the start of a step. In this model a step's duration is the SERIAL SUM of the compute of every request in it, so a request that arrives mid-step waits one whole quantum of prompt_tokens / 5,708 tok/s: 0.066 s at N = 1 and 0.186 s at N = 3, 2.8x more. The measurement does not behave that way. At C0 N = 3 10 %, where the simulator records NO step sharing at all, the simulated tail above the median is 0.173 s - 0.93 of one quantum - while the measured tail above the same median is 0.096 s, about HALF a quantum. A waiting request in the real engine is therefore released part way through the running prefill, which is what vLLM's V1 scheduler does: with an 8,192-token step budget it admits up to 7 requests of 1,062 tokens into ONE forward pass, and that pass is SUB-LINEAR in its tokens because a single 1,062-token prefill does not saturate the GPU. The model has no sub-linear batching term, so it over-charges every concurrent prefill by the sharer's own compute time. At N = 1 that error is 0.066 s and stays inside the +/-25 % band of a 0.45 s budget; at N = 3 it is 0.186 s against a budget only 2.7x larger, so the N = 3 cells fall outside it. This is an ABSENT link in the sense of CLAUDE.md Step 2, not a mis-set constant: StudyD7 and StudyD7b measured PER-REQUEST peaks (15.10 req/s at 378 tokens and 5.38 req/s at 1,062), and nothing committed measures BATCHED prefill throughput at either N. Correcting it would need that measurement, which this study does not have, so it is diagnosed and left alone.
n3_diagnosis.limits_of_this_diagnosis: Two things the table shows that the mechanism above does not fully explain. First, the same over-charge is present at N = 1: the simulated tail is 1.10 / 2.15 / 4.14 / 4.73 quanta at 10 / 25 / 40 / 50 % against a measured 1.09 / 1.92 / 3.61 / 4.32, so the model is 1 to 15 % long there too - it is only in SECONDS that N = 3 leaves the band. Second, the sign REVERSES at C0 N = 3 50 %, where the simulated tail is 3.48 quanta against a measured 4.27, so at the top of the N = 3 ladder the model under-queues instead. A single missing sub-linear batching term does not produce a sign reversal, so at least one further effect is present at high N = 3 load and is not identified here.
n3_diagnosis.what_would_fix_it: a committed measurement of prefill wall time against batch token count on the same server - for example StudyE10c's E0 configuration driven at a fixed concurrency of 1, 2, 4 and 8 simultaneous N = 1 and N = 3 prefills - which would give the engine a measured step-time curve instead of a linear one
